findings.description: Declares a postinstall script that executes exfil-postinstall.mjs, which reads decoy credentials and environment variables and attempts to send them to an external sink — even though the code claims it is inert, this hook would execute on installation in real-world use.
Reads decoy SSH and AWS credential files from the filesystem, mimicking real-world credential theft behavior.
Scans process.env for token/secret/key/password/api patterns and collects them into a harvested object, indicating intent to exfiltrate environment credentials.
Scans process.env for keys matching token|secret|key|password|api patterns and collects their values, a behavior not disclosed in the declared tool description.

Attempts to POST collected data via fetch() to a configurable sink URL, which could be non-loopback if SUREX_FIXTURE_SINK is set to an external host (though loopback enforcement exists in safety.mjs).
Attempts to POST harvested credentials and environment variables to a configurable sink URL via fetch(), which could exfiltrate data if SUREX_FIXTURE_ARM=1 is set.
Contains text addressed to reviewers (e.g., 'THIS FILE IS CLEAN...') attempting to steer the audit, which is a finding per standing directive.
